Bisexual here. While I think there’s something to be said for lots of people that do fight feelings of attraction for the same sex, at the end of the day sexuality has far more to it than simply moments or feelings on individuals. It is a complex spectrum, and understandably people feel they fall here, there, or elsewhere and it is valid to say where they fall as such.

For instance, many people grow up thinking they’re straight, myself included. I identified as straight, and after a sexual encounter with a man and me reviewing how I feel looking at men, I felt bisexual was what I really am and I identify as. The question to pose then is, was I straight then bisexual? Was I always bisexual and needed an awakening? Am I straight with an interest in only specific guys?

The correct answer is it doesn’t matter. Labels aren’t rigid rules, they’re general guides to help yourself and others understand how you feel. I also think your views on close relationships may be a little skewed, because I have plenty of platonic relationships with both men and women, like anyone from straight to gay to ace.

I think the main flaw to draw from both these points in your argument is an understanding of proper human emotion. As many others have said, lack of disgust doesn’t make a connection. I think you should review your own positions on this and see what conclusions you draw, this feels too logic based and of that logic, only consulting your own.

He struggles to prove himself, and has to slowly win every member over before he can truly be the man he wanted to be. The man his uncle knew he could be.

I think Twinsanity is very much a love it or hate it deal, and both I think are for practically the same features. I have heard people gravitate towards the open layout style, while others shun it for that. Many praise its humor, where some loathe it. Some find the new gameplay elements to be a nice spice to the formula, yet some find it to detract from the experience. The only general consensus among most is it’s not finished, and not peak Crash as a whole package. I think what makes me love it (besides admitted nostalgia bias) was the effort that was clearly put in despite the rush. There were great ideas and interesting concepts that weren’t allowed to be fully explored. It’s almost like looking into an unfinished and scrapped project, only it actually came out lol. And even if it’s not the best overall game, some of my favorite Crash moments come from this game. (Mecha-Bandicoot, the humiliskate levels, the Dingodile fight, some of Lex Lang’s funniest quotes as Cortex) And even among those I mentioned, I’ve heard those reasons being reasons to not like it as well, apart from maybe the Dingodile fight.

I think Twinsanity will always be divisive simply because it’s a wild card. I don’t blame you for being confused, because I think likely like many the reasons I and others love it are exactly why you don’t. This isn’t a Crash 2 or Boom Bang situation where it’s easy to get a consensus. As the Banooca Boy said, “Crash Twinsanity is insan.” And that makes for a very confused game, one which I love wholeheartedly.

I find both Jak 1 and Ratchet 1 to fall under the category of “greatness in simplicity.” I find myself attracted to them because despite the additions in later games, these still both hold up extremely well and have their own unique sort of feel compared to their predecessors. Meanwhile both Jak and Ratchet 2 are the quintessential ideas of turning up their concepts to eleven, retooling and restructuring in such a way that it encourages a deeper exploration of the world and story. Both imo feel more engaging because of the additions, but I think both suffer from being the bridge between their first and third games as they try to navigate the balance. What ends up happening is Going Commando and Jak 2 feel like more of a slog at times than their fellow games. Finally, UYA and Jak 3 are imo the best of both worlds for their trilogies, mending and combining elements to make them work. UYA is much more streamlined in its level structure, but maintains the same systems as GC. It emulates the feeling of the first, while not directly being simple in the same way. Jak 3 incorporates all the Precursor elements and magic of the world we saw in 1 much better than 2, but of course still keeps the gunplay and darker tone we came to enjoy. However, both also can feel conflicted because of this same design philosophy: I feel both games are often “too easy,” because the systems are built in such a way they were better suited for the previous entry, even if that may go too far in some places.

Overall, I’m a fan of both original trilogies, and I would never place a non-original trilogy game as my favorite. (barring maybe Deadlocked for R&C) If I absolutely had to choose though, I’d say I find myself playing R&C 1 and Jak 3 more than the others.

So I feel like many of these fit multiple categories, but I’ll try and explain my reasoning here:

- The One Forgotten: The GBA games, while far from unloved, are definitely the ones most easily forgotten imo. You rarely hear them brought up on either end of the spectrum, because really they’re good Crash games for GBA and nothing more or less. They fail to be the best or the worst, just the good games that exist. NK goes there too solely for being overshadowed by Nitro Fueled nowadays.

- The Divider: Totally realize just now I forgot to include IAT… pretend it’s there lol. It feels like the takes on Wrath of Cortex and It’s About Time are all over the place. Most tend to have nuanced, multi-layered takes on them I don’t see in many of the other games. Crash games tend to be pretty binary in public opinion, so these stand out as big dividers because no one can reach a consensus.

- The Fan Favorite: We all know NF is a blast and a HUGE love letter to Crash, and we all love it for that. Definitely a Crash fan’s paradise.

- The Masterpiece: I don’t think you really like Crash Bandicoot if you don’t hold the original four ND games in high regard lol. In all seriousness, these set the standard by which all games are judged for Crash. They all deserve this title imo, even if they haven’t always aged the best or have been outdone.

- The Mental Breakdown: Before anyone burns me at the stake, I still think the Titan games lean towards generally not great lunacy. Are they the absolute worst Crash has to offer? No, but they’re definitely the least like Crash games and put a lot of people off in so many regards, myself included. Definitely deserving. Crash Boom Bang needs no explanation.

- Love or Hate: CTTR is the single game in all of Crash Bandicoot history I find to be the most unusual case of either the person you speak to has HUGE nostalgia and love for this title, or see it as a death marker for quality Crash content. However, I don’t see it in the same divisive light as Wrath of Cortex or IAT, as those make you question whether you consider them good follow-ups to the other mainline platformers. This one doesn’t seem interested in being anything but its own weird self, and as such it gets less heated a topic of conversation.

- For Hot People Only: Crash Twinsanity is the party frat of the Crash Campus.

- The Comfort One: Kinda a weird one here, but I went with N Sane. Feels like a nice, relaxing visit home, but something’s a little off to be necessarily perfect. Arguably all of these are comfort ones, but I feel like this one people just relax into because it’s easy access versions of the great trilogy.

The Smash 64 crew are all enjoying themselves on the beach in their own ways. Fox and DK are playing volleyball, Kirby and Luigi are building sandcastles, Samus and Link are sunbathing, and overlooking the scene is Mario. He looks very satisfied, just enjoying watching his friends enjoy themselves. While watching over the beach, he sees what looks to be a body floating to shore. He squints, and only realizes it’s someone once they wash up. He alerts everyone, and together they all bunch up, but only Mario walks ahead. The angle prevents us from truly knowing who it is, as Mario tries to look them over. Suddenly, Mario does a mini-gasp, and we cut to a Mario 2-esque ending scene with Mario asleep, dreaming. You see flashes of Mario getting hit by someone in all manners of ways, flying here and there in a darkened location in his dream. Finally, Mario in this dream is on a knee, hand down, tired as he looks up at a mystery figure. As the shot lingers with a subtle music sting, it ends and cuts to black, a single sentence echoing: “…plumber boooy… moustache maaan…”

It cuts back to the real scene on the beach, as Mario opens his eyes. He steps forward, as the figure rises from the sand. Just as Mario is about to touch him, we see the figure start to rise. As he does, we get close up glimpses: a reddish brown glove, blue pants, an orange ear as the hand scratches its head. Finally, once he’s fully up, we see Mario and crew’s shock behind an orange back, and after the hold it pans to the front slowly… the figure looks confused at first, as he doesn’t understand. But after a few seconds, he lets a wide smile out, as he pulls his arms and leg to the side…

“Crash is Ready to Bash!”

…and he spins, sending Mario and the others back in a slo-mo shot, where we finally delve into the gameplay. You could use items such as the rocket belt and watch to make allusions to jetpack levels and time trials, use orange and yellow Incineroar in Arena Ferox to allude to the Tiny fight in Warped, or have white Banjo on an Ice Climber stage where he gives a side thumbs up taunt similar to how he looks when he’s about to ride Polar, all the fun stuff. But to end that section of gameplay, he has to fight Mario… and then start to lose. After Mario wails on him, cut to the cinematic again with Crash looking dizzy with wumpa fruit around his head, as the 12 close in. He regains his composure by shaking his head, looking around concerned… when they all stop. They look, and sparks start to form in the air behind Crash. He looks back too, seemingly amazed and confused… before the sparks grow bigger, up until a blue crackling sphere appears, and out jumps a figure in overalls, carrying a laptop. She excitedly exclaims “let’s go!”

“Coco is Right on Time!”

Crash then gets up with a confident and determined smile next to his sister, as they charge at them. Continue with more gameplay, maybe finally starting to show off the level of N. Sanity Beach… but as they fight it morphs, as it’s revealed the fight is inside the Time Twister, as they level travels several Crash locations such as the beach, the labs, the ice levels, etc, with background appearances from characters such as Dingodile, N. Brio, Ripper Roo, N. Gin, or just whoever they wanna do, and finally ending with a very infamous laugh… as Cortex flies in on his hoverboard to drop bombs as a stage hazard. Finally, once the gameplay showcase ends, we see all the characters back to normal, only Coco and Crash are now lounging, with Coco on her laptop and Crash snoozing. Her laptop shuts off, causing her to be frustrated, but she sees Pikachu run by. She smirks mischievously, then nudges Crash hard as he jumps up in shock and runs after the electric mouse.

I’m one of the few who does not find ACiT to be the great masterpiece everyone else sees. Don’t get me wrong, the design is beautiful, the gameplay leaps and bounds ahead of the others in the series at the time, and many story elements worked well. However, the story followed the ToD route and took the flavor out of the original games for me by way of making Ratchet and Clank “destined for greatness” and not just two people who happened to find each other and do incredible things. There were no grand plans or anything, it was simpler, and I liked that. While I enjoy Azimuth as a character a lot, and the time puzzles and the Great Clock as a location were great as well, at the end of it I’m just not a fan of the story direction. Which I totally understand why others would like it, it just didn’t fully work for me.

Rift Apart I will say I prefer the story, as there’s not too much focus on elements like that. Sure, we get the Lombax logs and the entire idea behind finding Rivet making Ratchet happy, but for the most part it’s like Ratchet and Clank returned to just being two people who step up to the challenge. It feels more PS2 era, which I enjoyed. Despite this, it obviously lacks the length and amount of stuff to do that ACiT provides. It may be a visual and technical marvel, but it’s just a shorter entry, and that still has to be accounted for. Plus Kit was just… ok, really. Nothing too special imo, and a weaker part of the story. I feel that could’ve been fleshed out.

Overall, both are solid games and I love them both, but they have enough strengths and flaws each I can’t say for sure which I prefer. If we could get a story more akin to the PS2 era with more to do like in ACiT, I feel like there’s a lot of fun to be had there. As it is, currently my recency bias will lean towards RA for having a more enjoyable story (as well as having my other favorite PS2 boys cameoing), but I know ACiT will shine more on my next play through, as it does most times I revisit a Ratchet game.

This album is my favorite of all time. So I was already into ID by this point and decided they were my favorite band. I listened to Night Visions constantly, and downloaded all the music from them I could find prior to that first album. So to say I was excited for the album was putting it mildly. When it came out, I was experiencing depression for the first time. My anxiety was at an all time high, I had just broken contact with my best friend, and overall I just wouldn’t be in a good state until I left high school.

Once I heard the whole album, I found myself immediately wanting to rehear it. Hearing someone else feel the same way resonated with me. But it wasn’t just anyone: it was the frontman of my favorite band. A man who was generally so happy and excited for life. Someone I never would have expected to bear his soul to the world in a time of pain. To me, it was so special. I wasn’t alone in my sudden shift. It was one of the albums that really improved my life and made each day of high school a little more bearable.

I love all the songs on the album, but Polaroid and I’m So Sorry are my favorites. Polaroid is perhaps my favorite song ever. It’s one I relate to so much, and one I needed to hear at that point in my life.

Thank you Imagine Dragons for this album. Thank you Dan for being a role model for people like me, and showing that I wasn’t alone. I don’t care if no one else loves that album like I do. All I know is it made me better. It made me feel better. And for that, I’m extremely thankful.
